title: Ordinal Day of a Date
statement:
You get a valid calendar date as a string date in the form "YYYY-MM-DD". Return which day of its year it is: January 1 is day 1, January 31 is day 31, February 1 is day 32, and so on.

Use the Gregorian leap-year rule: a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100, which are leap years only if they are also divisible by 400. In a leap year February has 29 days.

examples.why: 31 days of January plus 28 of February, then the 1st: 31 + 28 + 1.
2024 is a leap year, so February has 29 days.
1900 is divisible by 4 but also by 100 and not by 400, so it is not a leap year.

constraints: date is a valid date between "1600-01-01" and "2400-12-31"
date has the form "YYYY-MM-DD" with leading zeros
hints: Split the string into year, month and day numbers.
The answer is the day of the month plus the lengths of all earlier months in that year.
Only February changes length, and only in leap years. Get the leap rule right for years like 1900 and 2000.

explain.intuition:
The day number is the days of the month so far plus the full months before it. Keep a table of month lengths, sum the entries before the given month, and add the day.

The only trap is February. The leap rule has three layers: every 4th year, but not every 100th, but again every 400th. So 2024 and 2000 are leap years, while 1900 and 2100 are not. It is easy to know this and still write only the first layer, which is why the tests include century years.
steps: Decide whether year is a leap year: (y % 4 == 0 and y % 100 != 0) or y % 400 == 0.
Build the month-length table with February set to 29 or 28.
Return day plus the sum of the first month − 1 lengths.
pitfalls: Writing only year % 4 === 0. That calls 1900 and 2100 leap years.
Adding the length of the current month as well, which counts it twice.
Using a date library and its time zone. new Date("2023-03-01") is parsed as UTC, and local-time getters can shift it to the day before.

solutions.title: Month-length table
solutions.idea: Add up the lengths of the earlier months, with a 29-day February in leap years, then add the day.

solutions.title: Cumulative table
solutions.idea: Precompute how many days come before each month in a normal year; add one for dates after February in a leap year.

followups: Return the number of days between two dates.
Go the other way: given a year and a day number, return the date string.
